t: After victory at Sekigahara, the Tokugawa shoguns ruled Japan from Edo from 1603 to 1868, keeping some 260 daimyo in check.
Two and a half centuries of peace produced a commercial economy, a city of a million in Edo, and arts like kabuki and ukiyo-e.
Unable to resist Perry's 'Black Ships' or the rising domains of Satsuma and Choshu, the last shogun handed power back to the emperor in 1867.
dyk: After the Shimabara Rebellion of 1637-1638, Japan under the Tokugawa saw no major warfare for more than two centuries.
ev: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeats Ishida Mitsunari's western coalition at Sekigahara
The imperial court appoints Ieyasu shogun
The siege of Osaka Castle destroys the Toyotomi house
Iemitsu formalises sankin-kotai, the alternate attendance of daimyo in Edo
Dutch traders are confined to the artificial island of Dejima in Nagasaki
Commodore Perry's 'Black Ships' enter Edo Bay demanding open ports
Shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu returns governing authority to Emperor Meiji
Imperial rule is restored and the Boshin War begins at Toba-Fushimi
